**#156 after-deploy: +0 recorded daemon launches/60.001949 s; no detector skips/tells or stall records observed. Capture counts and round latency are not exposed.**

Reported deployment and canonical checkout: `d4846c1ca758ba6d543297fd6d7177503d752cb1`. Daemon PID **38000**, process start **2026-11-08 03:39:05 +10:00**, unchanged across snapshots; store **user_version 42**. Ping's generic build label does not independently identify the deployed Git SHA.

Two pings: **03:49:00.809405 to 03:50:00.811680 +10:00**, **60.001949 s** monotonic elapsed.

| Measurement | Result |
|---|---|
| Daemon launches | **140 to 140: +0, 0.000/s**; all ten populated sites flat |
| Registration counters | **10 attempts / 13 ps**, unchanged |
| Interval CPU | **7.17 CPU seconds / 60.001949 s = 11.95%** of one CPU |
| RSS | **173.95 to 174.00 MiB**, +48 KiB |
| Machine launches | **42.5/s**, separate niced 20-second sample |
| Detector metadata since boot | **0 audited skip events, 0 tell-outcome events, 0 stall rows/open rows/recorded accepted recipients** |
| Claude outcomes since boot | **0**; F82 traffic-bearing proof still pending |

Detector metadata was read at **03:51:03.166 +10:00**, covering this PID's boot onward, including the full ping window. Indexed seat/kind/time queries used the source's `watchdog.modal-stall` constant and the fixed `modal-stall-skipped` outcome. A fresh `report.now` event was the positive control through the same index/filter shape.

**Proof limit:** this is not a measured zero-capture fleet. A healthy capture that finds no dialog, or a matching dialog with no owed recipients, produces no detector audit. Failed attempt admission can appear in tell-outcome metadata without sending. There is no persisted round-start/end or elapsed metric in the watchdog/tick loop, so neither total captures per round nor actual round latency can be recovered here. The source schedules nominal 60-second ticks and awaits each action; that is not a latency measurement. No synthetic modal, capture probe or timing instrumentation was introduced.

CPU is close to the earlier #149 window's 12.02%, but different daemon incarnations/workloads prevent attributing that difference to #156. Flat launch counters likewise do not measure detector query/capture work.

The machine sample attributed **42.4/s** as a lower bound: **20.7/s other**, **21.7/s gone before identification**, no recognized daemon-child contribution. It made **257,453 in-process polls** in 20 seconds and consumes CPU despite nice priority. Its interval/scope differs from the daemon minute. The first attempt found no justfile in the sparse governance checkout; the successful sample ran from the canonical product checkout.

Raw session receipts: `pr156-after-window.json`, `pr156-after-machine.json`, `pr156-after-detector-before.json`. Store reads were metadata-only and read-only; no message bodies, credentials, tests, builds, restart or model traffic.
